name: Release Plan
one_liner: What will be released and when — the delivery strategy, not a calendar.
purpose: The Release Plan documents the high-level UX and development milestones, giving information on what will be released and when, based on what the Project Core Team knows at a given point in time. It results from the initial overall planning effort during the PM² Initiating and Planning phases and is adjusted with progress and feedback from the A-PCT. Releases introduce a timeboxed rhythm to construction, give stakeholders some predictability, and let the plan carry the dependencies, transition and business implementation activities each release needs.

fields.what: The Release Plan's focus is primarily on what needs to be done and when — the iteration level covers how.
fields.pollux: Four releases in 2029: member-state view, instrument and reconciliation, scenario overlay, self-service builder.

fields.what: Documents the high-level UX and development milestones; the glossary calls this the Release Schedule.
fields.pollux: 29 Mar, 28 Jun, 27 Sep, 20 Dec 2029 — the same dates as the Charter milestones.

fields.what: Plans the release of usable versions of the solution — releases exist to put working solution in users' hands.
fields.pollux: Release 1 is read-only exposure by member state — thin, but genuinely usable by the Board Secretariat.

fields.what: A high-level plan with the main goals to be achieved, including the major features to deliver.
fields.pollux: Release 2 goal: Risk and Finance stop maintaining their own spreadsheets (SC3).

fields.what: Offers visibility to the risks, issues, decisions, changes, constraints and assumptions related to the development aspect.
fields.pollux: Dependency: no CASTOR schema change during the Release 2 window.

fields.what: Assists scheduling transition activities such as deployment strategy and activities, documented and aligned with the PM² Transition Plan.
fields.pollux: Cut-over rehearsals two weeks before each release; service transition completed 31 Jan 2030.

fields.what: Releases reaching the whole requestor organisation carry Business Implementation activities aligned with the PM² Business Implementation Plan.
fields.pollux: National-authority training and access onboarding scheduled before Release 3 on 27 Sep 2029.

fields.what: Releases introduce a timeboxed rhythm to construction, providing some level of predictability for the team and stakeholders.
fields.pollux: Roughly quarterly releases over six two-week iterations each.

fields.what: Facilitates management of dependencies the system has with other projects, information systems or operations activities.
fields.pollux: The single upstream dependency is the CASTOR nightly extract owned by Lending Operations.

fields.what: The AGB wants releases and major objectives; the PrOw needs which work items land in which release.
fields.pollux: De' Medici's board pack shows four releases and their objectives; Curie's view shows every item.

fields.f: Build it as early as possible
fields.what: Hold the first Release Planning ceremony to establish the initial plan as soon as possible, preferably early in Planning.
fields.pollux: First Release Planning on 23 Oct 2028, a week after the RfP gate.

fields.what: It reflects the whole release strategy — marketing, operational, economic, legal — not just dates and functionality.
fields.pollux: National-authority access waits for Release 3 because the legal basis had to be confirmed first.

fields.what: New inputs from Iteration Review and Retrospective generate work items; updated velocity must be reflected in the plan.
fields.pollux: Velocity settled at 34 points after iteration 3; Release 4 scope trimmed accordingly.

fields.what: Its outputs update the plan: items added, updated or removed with the relative estimates given by the team.
fields.who: PrOw R/A for the ceremony · TeCo supports
fields.pollux: Held at least once per iteration; Curie runs it, Lovelace facilitates, Einstein defends enablers.

fields.what: WIL size and team velocity together evaluate feasibility; different data sets create optimistic and pessimistic scenarios.
fields.pollux: Pessimistic velocity of 28 points showed Release 4 slipping; scope was cut, not the date.

fields.what: Velocity and the pre-defined iteration size must be clearly visible and identified as the plan's current assumptions.
fields.pollux: Stated on the plan: two-week iterations, 34 points, team of eight with no holiday gaps assumed.

fields.what: Plan the production deployment strategy as early as possible — it can impact both the WIL and the Release Plan.
fields.pollux: Deployment dry-runs became enabler stories once operations named their cut-over window.

fields.what: BM I · PM A · TeCo R · PrOw S · ArOw S · ATeM S. BM is informed by the PrOw of the updated plan.
fields.pollux: Lovelace builds it, Curie supplies the delivery strategy, Hopper is informed of each update.

traps: Release Plan = what and when; Iteration Plan = how.
TeCo is Responsible, not the PrOw — the PrOw only Supports.
BM is Informed here but Supports on the Work Items List.
It is not the PM² Transition Plan — it schedules transition activities, not readiness.
A release strategy, not a date list: marketing, legal and operational drivers included.
